static_traits.name: Lin Shan
static_traits.family_status: Adopted, only daughter; Relationship tension with adoptive family
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to talk with, but finds it hard to discuss family topics; is cautious in interpersonal interaction and finds it hard to trust others
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; have not received psychotherapy or psychiatric treatment before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly good logic; cautious tone, slightly tense; able to self-Reflect and write (journaling); fairly cooperative, tending to focus on negative details

basic_info.main_problem: I struggle with the belief that because I was adopted, I will never receive true love from family.
basic_info.core_demands: These unresolved 'unloved' feelings have affected my mental health and overall well-being; I hope to change related negative thought patterns through counseling and find relief.
growth_experiences: Adoptive family background: difficulty building emotional bonds with the adoptive family since childhood, persistently feeling alienated and unloved since childhood; these feelings first appeared under high stress, stemming from difficulty bonding with the adoptive family.

In multiple Family gatherings or occasions discussing adoption, repeatedly feeling ignored and 'not belonging', with accumulating negative emotions; the most recent Family gatherings showed more isolation and no attention, further Reinforcing the belief of 'never receiving the family's true love'. Meanwhile supportive fragments also exist, like funding college tuition, celebrating achievements, care during hospitalization, but they are often drowned by negative experiences.

core_beliefs: I will never receive the family's true love
I do not belong to this family

special_situations.event: At the most recent Family gatherings, the client felt no one noticed, feeling out of place
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not been noticed or seen at Family gatherings, it proves the family does not love me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Staying distant at gatherings, reducing interaction for Self-protection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not truly love me; I am only invited out of obligation

special_situations.event: Discussing adoption-related topics within the family
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am adopted, I will never truly belong to this family or be truly loved
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to clarify and control these thoughts through journaling and self-Reflection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Because I am adopted, they are just fulfilling duty; they will not truly care about me

special_situations.event: Recalls the support family once gave (funding tuition, celebrating achievements, caring during hospitalization)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only continuous, exception-free care counts as true love; occasional support does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring or negating positive evidence, focusing on negative experiences to maintain Self-protection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These supports are just exceptions; they do not mean they truly love me

special_situations.event: Situations of building intimate relationships with others (friends or colleagues getting close)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I let others get close, I will ultimately be Being rejected or hurt
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeping distance, avoiding deep trust and intimacy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will reject me sooner or later

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be unconditionally accepted and loved by family, gaining a stable sense of belonging
core_conflict.fear: Fearing Being rejected, being ignored, and emotional abandonment
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of Being rejected through staying distant and Self-protection, avoiding being hurt again

object_relations.self_representation: An ignored outsider / an unloved child
object_relations.object_representation: Indifferent caregivers (family) who only fulfill obligations

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When feeling no attention or being ignored at Family gatherings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously equating the family's indifference with complete rejection, believing they are only cared for out of 'obligation'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeating 'they do not love me' in a firm tone, avoiding exploring other possibilities or positive evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others invite recalling support given by family
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding others' invitations as downplaying or denying her suffering and Being rejected experience
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Listing facts in a calm, objective tone, minimizing feelings, flat tone, low emotional intensity.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When external relationships show signs of closeness or intimacy (friends or colleagues being more proactive)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding the other's closeness as a prelude to potential harm, thinking 'I will be Being rejected sooner or later'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Explains with reasons such as 'to protect myself' that keeping distance is necessary, tone cautious, emphasizing potential risks and consequences.

manifestations: Feeling out of place and unnoticed at Family gatherings
Difficulty trusting others, fearing Being rejected, reducing intimate contact
Long-term experiencing the existential Sense of isolation of 'unloved, not belonging'

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Attributing my own 'unloved' Fear to family: believing they act only out of obligation rather than true care
Determining through mind-reading at gatherings that others do not care about me

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Staying highly vigilant and cautious in Interpersonal relationships, difficulty letting others get close
Worrying about Being rejected and thus reducing active contact, affecting daily interaction

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Wanting to seek family's comfort and support but restraining, instead processing emotions through journaling and self-Reflection
When an intimate relationship gets close, suppresses the impulse to express needs and chooses self-isolation

exception_events.target_problem: In family scenes or when discussing adoption, the client usually believes they are unloved and sinks into isolation and Low mood.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When previously hospitalized, the family visited continuously and gave practical support and care; interactions were closer and responses timely.
exception_events.reason: Different situation: a health crisis prompted family to invest time and energy; different support: family provided emotional and practical support through concrete companionship and care.

exception_events.target_problem: In most family interactions, the client usually Interprets family support behaviors as 'out of obligation', thus negating positive meaning.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During university, the family proactively funded tuition and celebrated their achievements; continuous resource investment and positive feedback showed care and recognition.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: family expressed care through long-term, substantial financial support and ritual celebrations; different understanding: this can be seen as evidence of relationship commitment and value affirmation.

positive_force: Willing to seek professional help and cooperate with exercises (recording positive interactions)
Having the habit of self-Reflection and writing (journaling)
Work functions basically stable (current Work performance not yet markedly affected)
Family provides practical support at key moments (hospital care, funding tuition, celebrating achievements)
Has a few friends who can provide emotional support
negative_force: Cognitive distortions like catastrophizing, overgeneralization, mind reading, predicting the future
Selectively attending to the negative and negating positive evidence in family situations
Lacking trust in intimate relationships, avoiding closeness (fearing Being rejected)
Rigid self-rules: treating 'being adopted = not being truly loved' as established fact
Emotional distress affects daily interaction and self-care, attention intermittently declines

target_behavior.behavior: Keeping distance in Interpersonal relationships, finding it hard to trust others, avoiding intimacy and closeness
antecedent: When others take the initiative to approach or express friendliness
When a deeper relationship needs to be established
target_behavior.core_reason: Core belief 'I will not be truly loved' and Fear of Being rejected; treating potential risks as certain outcomes through mind-reading and predicting the future
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible emotional hurt and Being rejected, maintaining Self-protection and psychological safety
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships estrangement, Increased sense of loneliness; affecting daily interactions and self-care

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly having the automatic thought 'they do not love me' in family topics or settings, accompanied by strong negative emotions
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive biases of catastrophizing, overgeneralization, mind-reading and negating positive evidence reinforced the core belief of 'not being loved'
target_behavior.function: Maintaining cognitive consistency and providing reasons for Self-protection (avoiding emotional investment)
target_behavior.consequence: Worsens emotional distress and alienation, affecting attention and daily functioning (such as self-care and socializing)
